equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at estimated fair value
equity_bridge.note: AMC BV 22.15% minority at ~$7bn Airtel Money IPO valuation (1,550) + other opco minorities at ~10x their $66m profit share (650). Book NCI is 340 (FY26 AR note). See inputs.nci_treatment.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2021-FY2026, USD reported, through the FY24-25 naira collapse)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.8% 5yr, -2.9% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (10.4%) and EPS (15.6%): the FX translation reserve absorbed the ~70% naira devaluation (FY24 PBT -63, FY25 ~$750m FX losses), so book value is not a usable growth anchor here. Owner-FCF CAGRs (38%/53%) are inflated by a depressed FY21-23 base (FY23 included $502m of spectrum capex) and by FY26 being a currency-recovery year; they are reported, not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - lease cash (principal + interest) - SBC - mobile-money float inflow; FY21-23 lease interest estimated at ~10% of average lease liabilities where the note is not in the KPI table (FY21 ~125, FY23 ~180). FY2021 owner FCF ~273, FY2023 ~384, FY2026 1,367. SBC is <0.1% of revenue in every year, so the SBC adjustment does not move any CAGR; the lease and float adjustments do.

scenario_narratives.base: Constant-currency growth stays in the low-to-mid teens as data (smartphone penetration ~50% rising toward ~79% by 2030) and Airtel Money (54m customers, TPV +35-50% cc) compound, while Nigeria's 2024/25 tariff uplift laps. Blended local currencies depreciate 6-8% a year against the dollar, so USD revenue grows 16% in FY27 (naira-recovery lapping) then 9% fading to 3%. The post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin holds near 50% through the energy-cost squeeze and gains ~1pp from mobile-money mix; tower lease cash eases from 11% to 10% of revenue with infrastructure sharing. Capex steps up to the guided $1.1bn plus spectrum and tapers to a 12.5% mature intensity. Cash tax normalises from 21% to 35% of lease-adjusted EBIT as the Nigeria FX-loss DTA is consumed and dividend WHT rises with upstreaming. Minorities are carried at the Airtel Money IPO mark.
scenario_narratives.bull: Currencies stabilise (naira held by orthodox CBN policy, East African currencies flat), so constant-currency growth converts almost fully into USD: +20% FY27, double digits for four years. Airtel Money's standalone listing re-rates the fintech franchise and its ~49% margins lift the group margin to 52%; the SpaceX direct-to-cell and Vodacom tower-sharing deals cut lease intensity to 9.5% and capex to 12%. Cash tax stays below the statutory blend as tax losses shelter Nigerian profits for longer and more cash is retained in-country for growth rather than upstreamed through WHT. Terminal growth 3.5% in USD.
scenario_narratives.bear: Another devaluation episode (naira and/or a Francophone or East African currency) in FY28 wipes a year of USD growth; thereafter USD revenue grows only ~3% as depreciation offsets volume. MTN/Safaricom price competition and diesel-driven site costs push the EBITDA margin to 46.5%; USD-indexed tower contracts raise lease cash to 12.5% of a smaller USD revenue base. Capital controls trap cash in opcos, so irrecoverable WHT and unrelieved losses lift the cash tax rate to 38%. Capex intensity stays at 13% to defend share. Growth of 1-3% against an 11.5% USD discount rate leaves most of today's price resting on the terminal value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Airtel Africa is valued as a USD-reporting operating telecom plus fintech on an owner-FCF basis: post-IFRS-16 EBITDA less the full tower lease cash, SBC (immaterial), D&A ex right-of-use for tax, a cash tax rate that ramps to the statutory-plus-WHT blend, guided capex plus spectrum, and a modest working-capital capture that excludes mobile-money float. Lease liabilities stay out of net debt because the lease is charged in the flows; minorities (18% of profit, Airtel Money 22% minority at its IPO mark) are deducted once in the bridge. Currency devaluation is charged in the USD growth path and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into WACC. The Airtel Money IPO at ~$7bn (nearly half the group's market value for ~21% of revenue) is a sum-of-parts marker that supports the bull case; it is not a cash windfall in the model.
key_risks_to_valuation: Local-currency devaluation vs USD (naira, and Francophone/East African currencies): a 1% blended USD move is ~$30m of EBITDA; the bear scenario assumes one more devaluation episode, a second would sit below it
Lease cash is 10.5-11% of revenue and partly USD-indexed: tower contract renewals at higher rates compress the lease-adjusted margin even when reported EBITDA margin holds
Cash tax convergence: the model ramps cash tax from 21% to 35% of EBIT; if DTA consumption and dividend WHT bite faster, FY28-30 FCF is lower than projected
NCI fair value is an estimate anchored on the Airtel Money IPO price; a re-rating of the listed subsidiary raises the minority deduction as well as the sum-of-parts
Nigeria regulatory/tariff risk on ~25% of revenue and capital controls on upstreaming cash to the plc
Terminal value carries most of the equity value at an 11.5% USD WACC; +/-1pp in WACC moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular LSE close, GBp); 52-week range 219.0-436.2; GBPUSD=X 1.3240 same date
data_sources.financials: AAF.L_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2026 annual, H1/9M/Q1 interims) from the DuckDB core_metrics; FY2026 Annual Report (cash flow statement, lease note, NCI note 'Interests in other entities', tax note, leverage table) and Q1 FY2027 trading update (23 Jul 2026) for shares repurchased and total net debt
data_sources.qualitative: AAF.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): FY2027 capex guidance ~$1.1bn, dividend policy, energy-cost margin caveat, Airtel Money IPO at ~$7bn with admission 14 Oct 2026, Bharti stake to ~79%

inputs.share_count_basis: 3,650.3m shares in issue at 31 Mar 2026 less 10.2m repurchased and cancelled to 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY27 update) = 3,640.1m, plus 7.1m dilutive awards (FY26 AR note 14, diluted EPS table) = 3,647m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (immaterial, ~$3m) is expensed in the flows; the remaining ~$63m of the $110m buyback to Nov 2026 is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company's lease-adjusted net debt at 31 Mar 2026 (FY26 AR p49 leverage table): borrowings 1,169 non-current + 1,019 current + 8 processing costs + 25 payment-service-bank customer deposits, less cash 646, term deposits 189, current investments 20 = 1,366. Lease liabilities (4,224) EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). Mobile-money trust cash of 1,394 excluded from cash because it is customer float with a matching liability. Q1 FY27 (30 Jun 2026) reports total net debt of 5,739 incl. leases (+149 in the quarter) without a lease split; the ex-lease movement is ~$0.03/share and is not restated.
inputs.owner_fcf_bridge: reported FCF (OCF 3,195 - capex 875) 2,320, less lease cash 671 (principal 204 financing + lease interest 467, FY26 AR note on leases), less SBC 3, less mobile-money wallet float inflow 279 (customer cash inside OCF, FY26 cash flow statement) = 1,367 owner FCF. Component build cross-check for FY26: EBITDA 3,162 - lease 671 - SBC 3 - D&A ex-ROU 628 = EBIT 1,860; cash tax 395 (21.2%); + D&A 628 - capex 875 + WC ex-float 122 = 1,341, within noise of 1,367.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income $27m is NOT stripped: the company is a net borrower (lease-adjusted net debt 1,366) and interest received (23) sits in investing activities, outside reported FCF already.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash-flow note 'Share-based payment 3 (FY25: 5)'; equity-award taxes nil. The Metrics.csv carries 5 for FY2026, which is the FY25 comparative - immaterial at 0.05% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: FY26 financing outflow $74m (first $100m programme); $46.6m more by 30 Jun 2026 under the new $110m programme. Repurchaser: the flat count is being funded.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD; LSE quote in pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 USD = 100/1.324 = 75.53 GBp, GBPUSD=X 1.3240 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-02 close). Parity check: 3,647m shares x quote / 75.53 = USD market cap ~$14.9bn, consistent with the ~$2.9bn Bharti paid for 16.31% in Jun-2026 (~$17.6bn implied at that time, when the shares were higher). No USD dual listing to tie to; the Lagos (NGX) line is naira-quoted and not used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Rf ~4.1% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a scaled prepaid telco = 9.1% market cost of equity; plus ~3.5pp partial frontier country/repatriation premium (Nigeria ~25%, East Africa ~47%, Francophone ~28% of revenue) = ~12.5% cost of equity. Cost of debt: local-currency borrowings at 10.6% nominal (FY26) are ~6-7% in USD-equivalent terms after expected depreciation, ~4.5% after tax. Weights ~91% equity / 9% debt (lease-adjusted) -> WACC 11.5%. Risk is charged ONCE: expected currency depreciation is in the USD growth path (cc growth less 6-8pp), the probability weights carry the devaluation-episode scenario, and WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, both on the FY26 cash-flow statement/lease note: 204 + 467 = 671, 10.5% of revenue; FY27 contractual <1yr maturities 837) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (4,224) are excluded from net debt; D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation (1,047 - 419 = 628). Tower contracts (3-15 yr composite leases with IHS/ATC/Helios, partly index/USD-linked) are an operating input, not acquisition debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Deducted ONCE, in the equity bridge at estimated fair value; flows are 100% consolidated. NCI took 149 of 813 PAT in FY26 (18%) against book NCI of only 340. AMC BV (Airtel Money) minority 22.15% (TPG Rise, Mastercard, Qatar Holdings, Chimetec) valued at the Oct-2026 IPO mark of ~$7bn -> 1,550; other minorities (Malawi 20%, a 49%-held opco, Uganda/Tanzania/Niger/Congo) earn ~66 of profit -> ~650 at ~10x. Total 2,200. The IPO itself is treated as value-neutral at a fair price (cash in / minority up); its relevance is the sum-of-parts mark, not a cash windfall.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating telecom + mobile money), routed via dcf-methods with the non-US adaptations (a) dual currency USD/GBp, (b) lease treatment B, (c) NCI in bridge, (f) risk charged once. Fresh build - no prior DCF or memory entry. EBITDA margin paths are the company's post-IFRS-16 underlying EBITDA margin (49.3% FY26, 50.1% Q1 FY27); lease cash is a separate deduction. Reported USD growth is constant-currency growth net of expected local-currency depreciation: FY27 base +16% reflects Q1 FY27 +31% reported (naira recovery lapping) fading through the year. Capex path adds ~0.7pp of revenue for spectrum/licence renewals, which the $1.1bn FY27 guidance excludes (FY23 spent $502m on intangibles). Working-capital capture is 5% of the revenue change: the FY26 reported inflow of 401 included 279 of mobile-money float that is not owner cash. Cash tax ramps 24% -> 35% of lease-adjusted EBIT: FY26 cash tax was 21% while book tax was 43% (blended statutory 32% + dividend WHT + unrecognised losses), with the Nigeria FX-loss DTA (428) being consumed. SBC-near-zero market: house and street bases are within 0.5% of each other; band_position is reported but carries no information.

base.growth_note: FY27: Q1 +31% reported / +21% cc; naira-recovery lapping fades through H2 -> ~16% for the year. Thereafter constant-currency low-to-mid teens (data +35% cc, mobile money TPV +35-50% cc, tariff lapping in Nigeria) net of 6-8pp blended depreciation -> 9% fading to 3%.
base.margin_note: Post-IFRS-16 underlying margin held near the FY26 49.3% / Q1 FY27 50.1% level in FY27-28 (energy-cost headwind flagged by the CFO) then +1pp from mobile-money mix; lease cash eases from 11% to 10% of revenue with Vodacom infrastructure sharing and revenue scale.
base.capex_note: FY27 guidance ~$1.1bn ex spectrum = 14.8% of projected revenue + ~0.7pp spectrum -> 15.5%, tapering to a 12.5% mature telco intensity. D&A ex-ROU rises from 9.8% toward 12% as the capex step-up depreciates.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 21% of lease-adjusted EBIT in FY26 vs 32% blended statutory plus dividend WHT; DTA consumption and rising upstreaming take the cash rate to 35% by FY33.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the naira fell ~70% in two years through FY25 and each 1% USD move costs ~$30m of EBITDA, Nigeria is ~25% of revenue under a single regulator, and FX repatriation limits are a live constraint - the downside axis is structural, not cyclical. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs currency stability, a sustained Airtel Money re-rating and margin expansion through an energy-cost squeeze to coincide. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: automated-check-unreliable: known fx_rate direction conflict between dcf_engine.py (currency->quote_currency, i.e. USD->GBp here) and sanity_check.py (expects quote_currency->currency). The script multiplied the GBp price series by fx_rate=75.53 instead of dividing, inflating every historical and implied multiple by ~75.5x^2 territory for P/B and P/S (both divide a price by a USD-denominated quantity). See memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict.md. Hand-recomputed in sanity_check_note below; that recomputation is a genuine pass.

sanity_check_note.reason: fx_rate direction conflict (see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict.md); automated implied_multiples/historical_averages above are not usable.
sanity_check_note.method: GBp monthly close at each FY-end (31 Mar) from AAF.L_Prices.csv, divided by fx_rate=75.53 (USD->GBp, the dcf_engine.py / inputs.fx_rate convention) to get a USD price, x shares_outstanding for market cap, against core_metrics USD actuals. Historical FX rate not available per-period, so the current fx_rate is used throughout (same approximation as prior occurrences of this bug).
sanity_check_note.verdict: genuine pass -- implied P/E ~21-22x and P/B ~4.2x sit within the hand-bridged FY2021-FY2026 historical range (P/E 9-38x, P/B 1.1-4.9x), near the upper half but not exceeding any historical maximum. No driver changes made.
